spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m9p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Orders, Slots

VARIABLES grants, epoch, cap
vars == <<grants, epoch, cap>>

ActiveSlots == { s \in Slots : s <= cap }
Owners(s)   == { o \in Orders : <<s, o>> \in grants }

Init ==
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ epoch  = 0
    /\ cap    = 2

Assign(o, s) ==
    /\ s \in ActiveSlots
    /\ Owners(s) = {}
    /\ \A t \in Slots : o \notin Owners(t)
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {<<s, o>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap>>

Reconfigure(nc) ==
    /\ epoch < 2
    /\ nc \in Slots
    /\ epoch'  = epoch + 1
    /\ cap'    = nc
    /\ grants' = { g \in grants : g[1] <= nc }

Withdraw(o, s) ==
    /\ <<s, o>> \in grants
    /\ grants' = grants \ {<<s, o>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : Assign(o, s)
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : Withdraw(o, s)
    \/ \E nc \in Slots : Reconfigure(nc)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoSlotDoubleBooked == \A s \in Slots : Cardinality(Owners(s)) <= 1
====
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction that assigns numbered execution slots to resting orders; each slot represents one priority position in the match queue. Only slots up to the current capacity are active, and the exchange occasionally reconfigures capacity at runtime by opening a new auction epoch with a possibly different number of active slots. When an order is admitted, the matcher grants it one currently free active slot, but only if that order does not already hold a slot in the book. A reconfiguration bumps the epoch counter and releases every grant whose slot number now exceeds the new capacity, so those orders must re-compete in the next epoch. An order that holds a slot may also withdraw at any time, freeing its slot back into the active pool. The matcher never grants a slot that is already occupied, and it never assigns beyond the active capacity. Because grants and releases interleave with capacity changes, the concern is that a single execution slot could end up promised to two different orders at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no execution slot is ever held by more than one order at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m4p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Participants, Authorized, Cap, MaxSession

VARIABLES queue, session, execA, execB
vars == <<queue, session, execA, execB>>

Init ==
    /\ queue   = << >>
    /\ session = 0
    /\ execA   = {}
    /\ execB   = {}

Enqueue(p, t) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ p \in Participants
    /\ t \in 0..MaxSession
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [who |-> p, tok |-> t])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, execA, execB>>

ValidHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ Head(queue).tok = session
    /\ Head(queue).who \in Authorized

ExecuteA ==
    /\ ValidHead
    /\ execA' = execA \cup {Head(queue)}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, execB>>

ExecuteB ==
    /\ ValidHead
    /\ execB' = execB \cup {Head(queue)}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, execA>>

DropHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ (Head(queue).tok # session \/ Head(queue).who \notin Authorized)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, execA, execB>>

Rotate ==
    /\ session < MaxSession
    /\ session' = session + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, execA, execB>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Participants, t \in 0..MaxSession : Enqueue(p, t)
    \/ ExecuteA
    \/ ExecuteB
    \/ DropHead
    \/ Rotate

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyAuthorizedExecuted ==
    \A c \in (execA \cup execB) : c.who \in Authorized
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Participants = {alice, bob, mallory}
  Authorized = {alice, bob}
  Cap = 2
  MaxSession = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyAuthorizedExecuted
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network has two independent lock controllers that both draw commands from one shared, bounded command queue. Participants submit lock/unlock commands tagged with their identity and the session token they last saw; the queue applies backpressure and refuses new submissions once it is full. The system rotates its session token from time to time, which makes any command still carrying an older token stale. A controller executes the command at the head of the queue only when that command carries the current session token and comes from an authorized participant, recording it in that controller's own execution log. If the head command is stale or comes from an unauthorized participant, either controller may drop it from the queue without executing it. Rogue participants can still enqueue commands, so the danger is that a controller might execute a command from someone who is not authorized. Both controllers share the single queue but keep separate logs of what they actually executed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every command recorded in either controller's execution log was submitted by an authorized participant.

---- MODULE W4Od0m5p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Voters, Members, Quorum, Decisions

VARIABLES votes, committed
vars == <<votes, committed>>

CommittedIds == { c.id : c \in committed }

Init ==
    /\ votes = [ d \in Decisions |-> {} ]
    /\ committed = {}

Vote(v, d) ==
    /\ v \in Voters
    /\ d \notin CommittedIds
    /\ votes' = [ votes EXCEPT ![d] = votes[d] \cup {v} ]
    /\ UNCHANGED committed

Commit(d) ==
    /\ d \notin CommittedIds
    /\ Cardinality(votes[d] \cap Members) >= Quorum
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {[id |-> d, voters |-> votes[d], byAdmin |-> FALSE]}
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

AdminCommit(d) ==
    /\ d \notin CommittedIds
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {[id |-> d, voters |-> {}, byAdmin |-> TRUE]}
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

AdminReopen(d) ==
    /\ d \in CommittedIds
    /\ committed' = { c \in committed : c.id # d }
    /\ votes' = [ votes EXCEPT ![d] = {} ]

Next ==
    \/ \E v \in Voters, d \in Decisions : Vote(v, d)
    \/ \E d \in Decisions : Commit(d)
    \/ \E d \in Decisions : AdminCommit(d)
    \/ \E d \in Decisions : AdminReopen(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

QuorumBackedOrOverride ==
    \A c \in committed :
        c.byAdmin \/ (Cardinality(c.voters \cap Members) >= Quorum)
====
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler commits each room-assignment decision only after a quorum of the authorized scheduling board votes for it. Board members cast votes on the pending decisions, and outside parties can also try to cast votes, but only votes from genuine board members should count toward a quorum. A decision commits when at least the quorum number of board-member votes has accumulated for it, and the committed record retains the full set of voters that were on file. There is also a privileged charge-nurse admin who can override the process and commit a decision unilaterally in an emergency, without any quorum. To keep the schedule flexible, the admin may also reopen a previously committed decision, which clears it and its votes so the board can decide again. The worry is that a decision might commit without real authorization: too few board members, or padded with votes from people not on the board.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every committed decision was either an admin override or backed by at least a quorum of genuine board-member votes.

---- MODULE W4Od15m2p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Accounts, InitTotal, MaxAmt

VARIABLES bal, phase, prepared, tx
vars == <<bal, phase, prepared, tx>>

RECURSIVE SumOf(_)
SumOf(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN bal[x] + SumOf(S \ {x})

TotalShares == SumOf(Accounts)

Init ==
    /\ bal = [ a \in Accounts |-> IF a = 1 THEN 2 ELSE IF a = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 ]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ prepared = {}
    /\ tx = [ from |-> 1, to |-> 1, amt |-> 0 ]

Propose(f, t, k) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ f # t
    /\ k >= 1 /\ k <= MaxAmt /\ k <= bal[f]
    /\ tx' = [ from |-> f, to |-> t, amt |-> k ]
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ prepared' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED bal

Prepare(p) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ p \in {tx.from, tx.to}
    /\ p \notin prepared
    /\ prepared' = prepared \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, phase, tx>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ prepared = {tx.from, tx.to}
    /\ bal' = [ bal EXCEPT ![tx.from] = @ - tx.amt, ![tx.to] = @ + tx.amt ]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prepared, tx>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, prepared, tx>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f, t \in Accounts, k \in 1..MaxAmt : Propose(f, t, k)
    \/ \E p \in Accounts : Prepare(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SharesConserved == TotalShares = InitTotal
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Accounts = {1, 2, 3}
  InitTotal = 3
  MaxAmt = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SharesConserved
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction settles share transfers between broker accounts using a two-phase commit so that a match either fully applies or not at all. When a transfer is proposed, the exchange enters a voting phase naming the seller account, the buyer account, and the number of shares to move. Each of the two participating accounts must prepare (vote yes) before the transfer can commit; a participant may be slow to prepare but is assumed never to fail outright, so the coordinator simply waits. Once both participants have prepared, the commit atomically debits the seller and credits the buyer by the same amount, then the exchange returns to idle and is free to propose another transfer. At any point during voting the coordinator may instead abort, leaving all balances untouched. Shares are only ever moved between accounts, never minted or burned. The concern is that a bug in the commit could cause the total number of shares in the system to change.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of shares summed across all broker accounts always equals the initial total.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, Cap

VARIABLES loc, queue
vars == <<loc, queue>>

BlockFree(b) == \A t \in Trains : loc[t] # b
BusyTrains   == { t \in Trains : loc[t] # 0 }
Occupied     == { loc[t] : t \in BusyTrains }

Init ==
    /\ loc = [ t \in Trains |-> 0 ]
    /\ queue = << >>

Request(t, b) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ loc[t] = 0
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [train |-> t, block |-> b])
    /\ UNCHANGED loc

Grant ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ LET h == Head(queue) IN
        /\ loc[h.train] = 0
        /\ BlockFree(h.block)
        /\ loc' = [ loc EXCEPT ![h.train] = h.block ]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

DropHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ ~ BlockFree(Head(queue).block)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED loc

Leave(t) ==
    /\ loc[t] # 0
    /\ loc' = [ loc EXCEPT ![t] = 0 ]
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Request(t, b)
    \/ Grant
    \/ DropHead
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Leave(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoTwoTrainsPerBlock == Cardinality(Occupied) = Cardinality(BusyTrains)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  Blocks = {b1, b2}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoTwoTrainsPerBlock
nl:
A subway signalling system controls a pool of track blocks, where each block is a critical resource that at most one train may occupy at a time. Two independent dispatchers share a single bounded queue of block-entry requests. A train that is not currently on any block may request to enter a specific block; the queue applies backpressure and rejects the request when it is full. Either dispatcher may serve the request at the head of the queue: if the requested block is currently free and the train is still off-block, the dispatcher moves the train onto that block and removes the request. If the head request targets a block that is already occupied, either dispatcher may simply drop it. A train sitting on a block may leave at any time, freeing that block for others. The safety concern is that the two dispatchers, drawing from the same queue, could both move trains onto the same block and cause a collision.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no two trains ever occupy the same track block at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od6m6p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, Slots, TTL, MaxClock

VARIABLES leases, clock, cap
vars == <<leases, clock, cap>>

Init ==
    /\ leases = {}
    /\ clock  = 0
    /\ cap    = 2

Acquire(car, s) ==
    /\ s \in Slots /\ s <= cap
    /\ \A l \in leases : l.slot # s
    /\ \A l \in leases : l.car # car
    /\ leases' = leases \cup {[car |-> car, slot |-> s, exp |-> clock + TTL]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, cap>>

Expire(l) ==
    /\ l \in leases
    /\ l.exp <= clock
    /\ leases' = leases \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, cap>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leases, cap>>

Reconfigure(nc) ==
    /\ nc \in Slots
    /\ cap' = nc
    /\ leases' = { l \in leases : l.slot <= nc }
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Next ==
    \/ \E car \in Cars, s \in Slots : Acquire(car, s)
    \/ \E l \in leases : Expire(l)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E nc \in Slots : Reconfigure(nc)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleLease == \A l1, l2 \in leases : (l1.slot = l2.slot) => (l1 = l2)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {c1, c2}
  Slots = {1, 2, 3}
  TTL = 1
  MaxClock = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleLease
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper assigns hall-call service slots to elevator cars using time-limited leases. Each lease records which car owns which slot and an expiry deadline measured against a shared clock that ticks forward. A car may acquire a currently unleased active slot, taking a lease that expires a fixed number of ticks later, and each car holds at most one slot at a time. When the clock advances past a lease's deadline, that expired lease is dropped and its slot becomes free again. The building's dispatcher can reconfigure the number of active slots at runtime; any lease on a slot that is no longer within capacity is immediately released. A car may only lease a slot that is genuinely free, never one already held by another car. The concern is that two elevator cars could end up holding live leases on the very same service slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no service slot is ever covered by two distinct live leases at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od18m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Commands, Cap

VARIABLES buffer
vars == << buffer >>

Init == buffer = {}

Admit(m) ==
    /\ m \in Commands
    /\ m \notin buffer
    /\ Cardinality(buffer) < Cap
    /\ buffer' = buffer \cup {m}

Process(m) ==
    /\ m \in buffer
    /\ buffer' = buffer \ {m}

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Commands : Admit(m)
    \/ \E m \in Commands : Process(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BufferWithinCapacity == Cardinality(buffer) <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Commands = {m1, m2, m3}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BufferWithinCapacity
nl:
A smart-home door-lock controller holds pending lock/unlock commands in a bounded command buffer. Because commands arrive over an unreliable radio mesh, they can be delivered and processed in any order, so the buffer is treated as an unordered set of outstanding commands rather than a strict queue. A new command is admitted only when the buffer is not already at its capacity limit; if the buffer is full the controller exerts backpressure and refuses the command. The controller may process any outstanding command at any time, removing it from the buffer regardless of when it arrived. Commands can be re-issued later, so an identifier that was processed earlier may appear again. The whole point of the backpressure is to protect a fixed-size hardware buffer. The concern is that a flaw in the admission check could let the number of outstanding commands grow past the buffer's capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of outstanding commands in the buffer never exceeds its fixed capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od7m3p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Bays, InitTotal

VARIABLES cargo, leader
vars == <<cargo, leader>>

RECURSIVE SumOf(_)
SumOf(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN cargo[x] + SumOf(S \ {x})

Init ==
    /\ cargo = [ b \in Bays |-> IF b = 1 THEN 2 ELSE IF b = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 ]
    /\ leader = "none"

Elect(c) ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED cargo

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # "none"
    /\ leader' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED cargo

Move(f, t) ==
    /\ leader # "none"
    /\ f # t
    /\ cargo[f] >= 1
    /\ cargo' = [ cargo EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1, ![t] = @ + 1 ]
    /\ UNCHANGED leader

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Elect(c)
    \/ StepDown
    \/ \E f, t \in Bays : Move(f, t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ContainersConserved == SumOf(Bays) = InitTotal
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {k1, k2}
  Bays = {1, 2, 3}
  InitTotal = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ContainersConserved
nl:
A container-ship crane yard coordinates container moves through an elected leader crane. At any moment there is either no leader or exactly one; when there is no leader, any crane may stand for election and become the leader. The leader can step down (or fail over) at any time, returning the yard to a leaderless state from which a new leader is elected; a crane may be slow to take up leadership but is never permanently lost. Only the current leader may authorize moving a single container from one bay to another bay. Containers are only ever relocated between bays, never added to the yard or removed from it. The total number of containers in the yard is therefore fixed by whatever was present at the start. The concern is that a coordination bug during a move or a failover could cause a container to be duplicated or lost.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of containers across all bays always equals the initial total.

---- MODULE W4Od18m2p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locks, InitTotal, MaxAmt

VARIABLES keys, phase, votes, tx
vars == <<keys, phase, votes, tx>>

Init ==
    /\ keys = [ l \in Locks |-> 1 ]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ tx = [ from |-> 1, to |-> 1, amt |-> 0 ]

Propose(f, t, k) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ f # t
    /\ k >= 1 /\ k <= MaxAmt /\ k <= keys[f]
    /\ tx' = [ from |-> f, to |-> t, amt |-> k ]
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED keys

Prepare(p) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ p \in {tx.from, tx.to}
    /\ p \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<keys, phase, tx>>

ApplyMove ==
    keys' = [ keys EXCEPT ![tx.from] = @ - tx.amt, ![tx.to] = @ + tx.amt ]

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes = {tx.from, tx.to}
    /\ ApplyMove
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, tx>>

AdminCommit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ApplyMove
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, tx>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<keys, votes, tx>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f, t \in Locks, k \in 1..MaxAmt : Propose(f, t, k)
    \/ \E p \in Locks : Prepare(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ AdminCommit
    \/ Abort

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CreditsConserved == keys[1] + keys[2] + keys[3] = InitTotal
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Locks = {1, 2, 3}
  InitTotal = 3
  MaxAmt = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CreditsConserved
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network shares a fixed pool of digital key-fob credits across its lock units. Moving credits from one lock to another goes through a two-phase commit: a proposal names the source lock, the destination lock, and how many credits to move, putting the system into a voting phase. Both the source and the destination must prepare before a normal commit atomically debits the source and credits the destination by the same amount, after which the system returns to idle. A privileged home-admin can override the protocol and force the pending transfer to commit even if the two locks have not both prepared, which is still an atomic move of credits. During voting the coordinator may also abort, leaving all balances untouched. Credits are only ever shifted between locks, never created or deleted. The concern is that a flaw in either the normal commit or the admin override could change the total number of credits in the network.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of key-fob credits summed over all locks always equals the initial total.

---- MODULE W4Od10m6p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES owner, leaseEpoch, curEpoch, signal, adminOverride
vars == <<owner, leaseEpoch, curEpoch, signal, adminOverride>>

Init ==
    /\ owner = [ b \in Blocks |-> "none" ]
    /\ leaseEpoch = [ b \in Blocks |-> 0 ]
    /\ curEpoch = 0
    /\ signal = [ b \in Blocks |-> "stop" ]
    /\ adminOverride = [ b \in Blocks |-> FALSE ]

Acquire(t, b) ==
    /\ owner[b] = "none"
    /\ owner' = [ owner EXCEPT ![b] = t ]
    /\ leaseEpoch' = [ leaseEpoch EXCEPT ![b] = curEpoch ]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curEpoch, signal, adminOverride>>

SetGo(t, b) ==
    /\ owner[b] = t
    /\ leaseEpoch[b] = curEpoch
    /\ signal[b] = "stop"
    /\ signal' = [ signal EXCEPT ![b] = "go" ]
    /\ adminOverride' = [ adminOverride EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE ]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, leaseEpoch, curEpoch>>

AdminGo(b) ==
    /\ signal[b] = "stop"
    /\ signal' = [ signal EXCEPT ![b] = "go" ]
    /\ adminOverride' = [ adminOverride EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE ]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, leaseEpoch, curEpoch>>

Clear(b) ==
    /\ (signal[b] = "go" \/ owner[b] # "none")
    /\ signal' = [ signal EXCEPT ![b] = "stop" ]
    /\ adminOverride' = [ adminOverride EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE ]
    /\ owner' = [ owner EXCEPT ![b] = "none" ]
    /\ leaseEpoch' = [ leaseEpoch EXCEPT ![b] = 0 ]
    /\ UNCHANGED curEpoch

BumpEpoch ==
    /\ curEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ curEpoch' = curEpoch + 1
    /\ owner' = [ b \in Blocks |-> "none" ]
    /\ leaseEpoch' = [ b \in Blocks |-> 0 ]
    /\ signal' = [ b \in Blocks |-> IF adminOverride[b] THEN "go" ELSE "stop" ]
    /\ UNCHANGED adminOverride

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Acquire(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : SetGo(t, b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : AdminGo(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Clear(b)
    \/ BumpEpoch

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SafeGo ==
    \A b \in Blocks :
        signal[b] = "go" =>
            (adminOverride[b] \/ (owner[b] # "none" /\ leaseEpoch[b] = curEpoch))
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  Blocks = {b1, b2}
  MaxEpoch = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SafeGo
nl:
A subway signalling block system grants each track block to a train under a lease tied to the current configuration epoch. A train acquires a lease on a free block, stamped with the epoch in force at acquisition. Only a train holding a current-epoch lease on a block may set that block's signal to GO; a train whose lease was stamped in an older epoch is considered stale and may not act. A block's lease can be released at any time, which drops the lease and forces its signal back to STOP. The control center is a privileged admin that may override and set any block's signal to GO on its own authority, independent of leases. When the admin reconfigures the network by advancing the epoch, all existing leases become stale and are dropped, and every GO signal that rested on a lease (rather than an admin override) is forced back to STOP. The danger is that a block could show GO while backed only by a stale or absent lease and no admin override, letting an unauthorized train proceed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a block's signal is GO, it is either an admin override or backed by a current-epoch lease held on that block.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m5p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Agents, Quorum, CapVals

VARIABLES votes, dispatchLog, cap
vars == <<votes, dispatchLog, cap>>

Range(s) == { s[i] : i \in DOMAIN s }

Init ==
    /\ votes = [ b \in Bags |-> {} ]
    /\ dispatchLog = << >>
    /\ cap = 1

Vote(a, b) ==
    /\ b \notin Range(dispatchLog)
    /\ votes' = [ votes EXCEPT ![b] = votes[b] \cup {a} ]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatchLog, cap>>

Dispatch(b) ==
    /\ b \notin Range(dispatchLog)
    /\ Cardinality(votes[b]) >= Quorum
    /\ Len(dispatchLog) < cap
    /\ dispatchLog' = Append(dispatchLog, b)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, cap>>

Reconfigure(nc) ==
    /\ nc \in CapVals
    /\ cap' = nc
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dispatchLog>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents, b \in Bags : Vote(a, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Dispatch(b)

DispatchedAtMostOnce == Cardinality(Range(dispatchLog)) = Len(dispatchLog)
====
nl:
An airport baggage router sends each bag to an aircraft through an irreversible final-dispatch step: once a bag is dispatched onto a loading lane it is gone and cannot be recalled. Each dispatch must be authorized by a quorum of routing agents, who cast votes for individual bags. A bag may only be dispatched once it has collected at least the quorum number of votes and only when the router still has spare lane capacity. The number of active loading lanes changes at runtime as the ground crew reconfigures capacity up or down. A bag that has already been dispatched must never be dispatched a second time. The router keeps an append-only log of every dispatch it performs. The concern is that a race between voting and reconfiguration could cause the same bag to be dispatched more than once.

---- MODULE W4Od9m4p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Controllers, Authorized, Cap, MaxVer

VARIABLES queue, currentVer, applied
vars == <<queue, currentVer, applied>>

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ currentVer = 0
    /\ applied = {}

Enqueue(c, v) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ v \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [ctrl |-> c, ver |-> v])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<currentVer, applied>>

Apply ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ Head(queue).ctrl \in Authorized
    /\ Head(queue).ver = currentVer
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[ctrl |-> Head(queue).ctrl, ver |-> Head(queue).ver, admin |-> FALSE]}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED currentVer

AdminApply ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[ctrl |-> Head(queue).ctrl, ver |-> Head(queue).ver, admin |-> TRUE]}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED currentVer

DropStale ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ (Head(queue).ctrl \notin Authorized \/ Head(queue).ver # currentVer)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<currentVer, applied>>

Bump ==
    /\ currentVer < MaxVer
    /\ currentVer' = currentVer + 1
    /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA e : e.ver = currentVer + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED applied

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, v \in 0..MaxVer : Enqueue(c, v)
    \/ Apply
    \/ AdminApply
    \/ DropStale
    \/ Bump

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoUnauthorizedApplied ==
    \A r \in applied : r.admin \/ r.ctrl \in Authorized
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {c1, c2, rogue}
  Authorized = {c1, c2}
  Cap = 2
  MaxVer = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedApplied
nl:
A power-grid load shedder processes feeder-shedding requests from a single bounded work queue. Each request carries the identity of the controller that issued it and the configuration version it was built against; the queue applies backpressure and refuses new requests when it is full. The shedder applies the request at the head of the queue only when that request comes from an authorized controller and carries the current configuration version, recording the applied request. If the head request comes from an unauthorized controller or carries an out-of-date (stale) version, it is dropped without applying. A privileged grid operator acts as admin and may force the head request through regardless of authorization or version. When the operator bumps the configuration version, the queue is purged of every request that does not match the new version, so stale requests never linger. The danger is that a shedding request from an unauthorized controller could be applied through the normal (non-admin) path.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every non-override request that was applied came from an authorized controller.

---- MODULE W4Od11m8p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Jobs, Printers

VARIABLES coarse, heldBy
vars == <<coarse, heldBy>>

HoldsSomePrinter(j) == \E p \in Printers : <<j, p>> \in heldBy
PrinterFree(p)      == \A j \in Jobs : <<j, p>> \notin heldBy

Init ==
    /\ coarse = "none"
    /\ heldBy = {}

AcquireCoarse(j) ==
    /\ coarse = "none"
    /\ coarse' = j
    /\ UNCHANGED heldBy

AcquireFine(j, p) ==
    /\ coarse = j
    /\ ~ HoldsSomePrinter(j)
    /\ PrinterFree(p)
    /\ heldBy' = heldBy \cup {<<j, p>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED coarse

ReleaseCoarse(j) ==
    /\ coarse = j
    /\ coarse' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED heldBy

ReleaseFine(j, p) ==
    /\ <<j, p>> \in heldBy
    /\ heldBy' = heldBy \ {<<j, p>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED coarse

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : AcquireCoarse(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : AcquireFine(j, p)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : ReleaseCoarse(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : ReleaseFine(j, p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PrinterMutex ==
    \A p \in Printers :
        \A j1, j2 \in Jobs :
            (<<j1, p>> \in heldBy /\ <<j2, p>> \in heldBy) => j1 = j2
====
nl:
A print-shop job spooler uses a two-level (hierarchical) locking scheme. To use a specific printer, a job must first take the shop's single coarse-grained queue lock, and only while holding it may the job then take the fine-grained lock on an individual printer. Print-job submissions arrive as messages that can be picked up and served in any order, so the spooler may grant the coarse lock to whichever waiting job it chooses. Once a job holds a printer, it may release the coarse queue lock (freeing the queue for others) while continuing to hold its printer, print, and later release the printer. A job holds at most one printer at a time, and it may only take a printer that no other job currently holds. Because a job can keep a printer after giving up the coarse lock, the fine-grained printer lock is the real guarantee of exclusive access. The danger is that two jobs could end up holding the same physical printer at once and produce garbled output.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no physical printer is ever held by two different jobs at the same time.

    /\ UNCHANGED inCS

====

CONSTANTS
  N = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CriticalSectionMutex
nl:
A subway signalling system protects a shared junction (the critical resource) using a token ring over its control nodes arranged in a circle. Exactly one node holds the circulating token at any time. Only the node currently holding the token may move a train into the junction, and it may do so only when the junction is empty; when it is done it removes the train, leaving the junction empty again. The token may only be passed to the next node in the ring while the junction is empty, so a node cannot hand off the token while still occupying the junction. A privileged central controller acts as admin and may reposition the token directly to any node, and may also grant a node access to the junction on its own authority without that node holding the token, but only when the junction is currently empty. The overriding requirement is that the junction never holds more than one train. The danger is that some interleaving of token passing and admin overrides could place two trains in the junction at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one train occupies the shared junction at any time.

---- MODULE W4Od5m9p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Players, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES record, committed, pending, epoch
vars == <<record, committed, pending, epoch>>

Init ==
    /\ record = {}
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ epoch = 0

Submit(u) ==
    /\ u \in Players
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[id |-> u, snap |-> record]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committed, epoch>>

Apply(pr) ==

    /\ pr.snap = record
    /\ record' = pr.snap \cup {pr.id}
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {pr.id}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {pr}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

StaleDrop(pr) ==
    /\ pr \in pending
    /\ pr.snap # record
    /\ pending' = pending \ {pr}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committed, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ pending' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committed>>

Next ==

    \/ \E pr \in pending : Apply(pr)
    \/ \E pr \in pending : StaleDrop(pr)

NoLostUpdate == committed \subseteq record
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Players = {u1, u2}
  MaxEpoch = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker keeps a shared roster record of which players have joined the current match. Player-join events arrive as messages that can be received and processed in any order. To join, a client reads a snapshot of the current roster and submits a proposal to add its player id on top of that snapshot. The matchmaker applies a proposal using optimistic concurrency: it accepts the proposal only if the roster still equals the snapshot the proposal was built on, in which case it writes back the snapshot plus the new id and marks that id as committed. If the roster has changed since the snapshot was taken, the proposal is stale and is discarded, so the client must resubmit against a fresh snapshot. From time to time the matchmaker reconfigures into a new epoch, bumping the epoch counter and clearing all outstanding proposals. The danger is a lost update: a stale proposal overwriting the roster and dropping a player who had already been committed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every player id ever committed to the roster is still present in the roster.

---- MODULE W4Od10m2p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Interlockings

VARIABLES holders, phase, candidate, prepared
vars == <<holders, phase, candidate, prepared>>

Init ==
    /\ holders = {}
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ candidate = "none"
    /\ prepared = {}

Request(t) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ holders = {}
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ candidate' = t
    /\ prepared' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED holders

Prepare(i) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ i \in Interlockings
    /\ i \notin prepared
    /\ prepared' = prepared \cup {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, phase, candidate>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ prepared = Interlockings
    /\ holders' = {candidate}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<candidate, prepared>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, candidate, prepared>>

Release(t) ==
    /\ t \in holders
    /\ holders' = holders \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, candidate, prepared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Request(t)
    \/ \E i \in Interlockings : Prepare(i)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Release(t)

BlockExclusive == holders = {} \/ \E t \in Trains : holders = {t}
====
nl:
A subway signalling block system grants exclusive use of a shared junction block to one train at a time, using a two-phase commit across the two interlocking controllers that guard the junction. When the junction is free and idle, a train may request it, which opens a voting phase for that candidate train. Both interlocking controllers must prepare (vote yes) before the grant can commit; a controller may be slow to prepare but is assumed never to fail, so the coordinator simply waits for it. Once both controllers have prepared, the commit hands the junction to the candidate train. During voting the coordinator may instead abort, returning to idle without granting anything. A train that holds the junction may release it, freeing the junction for a future request. The overriding requirement is that the junction is never granted to two trains at once. The danger is that some interleaving of requests, votes, and commits could place two trains on the junction simultaneously.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared junction is held by at most one train at any time.

---- MODULE W4Od16m3p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Arms, Cap

VARIABLES leader, filled, crashed
vars == <<leader, filled, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ filled = 0
    /\ crashed = {}

Elect(d) ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<filled, crashed>>

Dispense ==
    /\ leader # "none"
    /\ filled < Cap
    /\ filled' = filled + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, crashed>>

Collect ==
    /\ filled > 0
    /\ filled' = filled - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, crashed>>

Crash(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {d}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = d THEN "none" ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED filled

Restart(d) ==
    /\ d \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, filled>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Arms : Elect(d)
    \/ Dispense
    \/ Collect
    \/ \E d \in Arms : Crash(d)
    \/ \E d \in Arms : Restart(d)

BinWithinCapacity == filled <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Arms = {d1, d2}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BinWithinCapacity
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser has several robotic dispensing arms that fill a single shared collection bin with pills. The arms elect one leader; only the current leader is allowed to drop a pill into the bin. The bin has a fixed physical capacity and must never be overfilled: a pill may be dispensed only while the bin holds fewer pills than its capacity. A patient may collect a pill from the bin at any time, lowering its count. Any arm can crash silently at any moment; if the crashed arm was the leader, the system is left leaderless until a new leader is elected from the arms that are still alive. A crashed arm may later restart and rejoin, becoming eligible for election again (failover). The danger is that a coordination fault lets the leader keep dispensing and overflow the bin beyond its capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of pills in the collection bin never exceeds its fixed capacity.

    /\ waiting = Cases
    /\ inRoom = {}
    /\ discharged = {}
    /\ epoch = 0

Admit(c) ==
    /\ c \in waiting
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
    /\ inRoom' = inRoom \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<discharged, epoch>>

Discharge(c) ==
    /\ c \in inRoom
    /\ inRoom' = inRoom \ {c}
    /\ discharged' = discharged \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, epoch>>

Return(c) ==
    /\ c \in discharged
    /\ discharged' = discharged \ {c}
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inRoom, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup inRoom
    /\ inRoom' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED discharged

    \/ \E c \in Cases : Discharge(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cases : Return(c)

CasesConserved ==
    Cardinality(waiting) + Cardinality(inRoom) + Cardinality(discharged) = RosterSize
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cases = {r1, r2}
  RosterSize = 2
  MaxEpoch = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CasesConserved
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler tracks a fixed roster of surgery cases as they move through the day. Every case is always in exactly one of three states: waiting to be scheduled, in a room, or discharged; no case is ever created or destroyed, so the three groups together always account for the whole roster. A waiting case is admitted into a room; a case in a room is later discharged. A room may be slow to admit its next case but is assumed never to fail, so the scheduler simply waits for it. A discharged case can be returned to the waiting list if the surgery needs to be redone. From time to time the scheduler performs an epoch-numbered reconfiguration, bumping the epoch and sending every case currently in a room back to the waiting list to be re-planned. All of these transitions merely move a case between the three groups. The danger is that a bug in one of these moves could duplicate a case or drop it entirely, so the groups no longer account for exactly the full roster.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of cases across the waiting, in-room, and discharged groups always equals the fixed roster size.

---- MODULE W4Od18m5p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Doors, Members, Quorum, Cap

VARIABLES unlocked, votes, crashed
vars == <<unlocked, votes, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ unlocked = {}
    /\ votes = [ d \in Doors |-> {} ]
    /\ crashed = {}

Vote(m, d) ==
    /\ m \notin crashed
    /\ d \notin unlocked
    /\ votes' = [ votes EXCEPT ![d] = votes[d] \cup {m} ]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unlocked, crashed>>

Unlock(d) ==
    /\ d \notin unlocked
    /\ Cardinality(votes[d] \ crashed) >= Quorum
    /\ Cardinality(unlocked) < Cap
    /\ unlocked' = unlocked \cup {d}
    /\ votes' = [ votes EXCEPT ![d] = {} ]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Lock(d) ==
    /\ d \in unlocked
    /\ unlocked' = unlocked \ {d}
    /\ votes' = [ votes EXCEPT ![d] = {} ]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Crash(m) ==
    /\ m \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unlocked, votes>>

Recover(m) ==
    /\ m \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unlocked, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members, d \in Doors : Vote(m, d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Unlock(d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors : Lock(d)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Crash(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Recover(m)

UnlockedWithinLimit == Cardinality(unlocked) <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Doors = {dA, dB}
  Members = {m1, m2, m3}
  Quorum = 2
  Cap = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT UnlockedWithinLimit
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network enforces a security policy that at most a fixed number of exterior doors may be unlocked at the same time. Unlocking any door requires a quorum of household members to vote for that specific door. Members cast votes for locked doors; a door is unlocked only once it has collected at least the quorum number of votes from members who are currently active, and only while the number of already-unlocked doors is below the allowed limit. When a door is unlocked its votes are cleared, and unlocking again later requires a fresh quorum. A door may be locked again at any time. Any member's controller can crash silently, and a crashed member's votes no longer count toward any quorum; a crashed controller may later recover and participate again. The danger is that a flaw could unlock a door while the limit of simultaneously-unlocked doors is already reached, exceeding the security capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of simultaneously unlocked doors never exceeds the allowed limit.

---- MODULE W4Od9m6p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Feeders, Budget, TTL, MaxClock

weight == [ f \in Feeders |-> IF f = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 2 ]

VARIABLES leased, exp, clock
vars == <<leased, exp, clock>>

RECURSIVE SumW(_)
SumW(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN weight[x] + SumW(S \ {x})

ShedWeight == SumW(leased)

Init ==
    /\ leased = {}
    /\ exp = [ f \in Feeders |-> 0 ]
    /\ clock = 0

Grant(f) ==
    /\ f \notin leased
    /\ ShedWeight + weight[f] <= Budget
    /\ leased' = leased \cup {f}
    /\ exp' = [ exp EXCEPT ![f] = clock + TTL ]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Expire(f) ==
    /\ f \in leased
    /\ exp[f] <= clock
    /\ leased' = leased \ {f}
    /\ exp' = [ exp EXCEPT ![f] = 0 ]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Restore(f) ==
    /\ f \in leased
    /\ leased' = leased \ {f}
    /\ exp' = [ exp EXCEPT ![f] = 0 ]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, exp>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Grant(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Expire(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Restore(f)
    \/ Tick

ShedWithinBudget == ShedWeight <= Budget

CONSTANTS
  Feeders = {1, 2, 3}
  Budget = 3
  TTL = 1
  MaxClock = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ShedWithinBudget
nl:
A power-grid load shedder sheds feeders under time-limited leases and must respect a total shed budget so it never sheds more load than allowed. Each feeder carries a load weight, and the shedder holds a budget that caps the combined weight of all feeders currently shed. To shed a feeder, the controller takes a lease on it, stamped to expire a fixed number of ticks in the future, but only if adding that feeder's weight keeps the combined shed weight within the budget. A shared clock ticks forward, and when a lease's deadline passes the lease is dropped and that feeder is restored, freeing up budget. An operator may also restore a shed feeder early. A feeder may be slow to be restored but is never lost. The danger is that a bug in the admission check could grant a lease that pushes the combined shed weight over the budget.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the combined load weight of all currently shed feeders never exceeds the shed budget.

CONSTANTS
  Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
  MaxRound = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyHolderPosted
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is coordinated by a token ring over the participating banks. Exactly one bank holds the settlement token at a time, and only the current token holder is authorized to post entries into the shared settlement batch during the current round. The token is passed around the ring to another active bank; each pass starts a fresh round in which the new holder is the only authorized poster, so any bank still assuming it holds the token from before is stale and must not post. The set of participating banks can change at runtime as banks join or leave, a capacity reconfiguration that bumps the round number, clears any in-round posting, and hands the token to a still-participating bank if the previous holder has left. The danger is that a bank which is not the current token holder, or is acting on a stale token from an earlier round, could post into the settlement batch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: in the current round, only the current token-holding bank has posted to the settlement batch.

---- MODULE W4Od12m4p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Fridges, InitTotal, CapVals

VARIABLES stock, queue, cap
vars == <<stock, queue, cap>>

SumOf(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN stock[x] + SumOf(S \ {x})

    /\ stock = [ f \in Fridges |-> IF f = 1 THEN 2 ELSE 0 ]
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ cap = 1

Enqueue(f, t) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < cap
    /\ f # t
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [from |-> f, to |-> t])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, cap>>

Process ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ stock[Head(queue).from] >= 1
    /\ stock' = [ stock EXCEPT ![Head(queue).from] = @ - 1, ![Head(queue).to] = @ + 1 ]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED cap

DropHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ stock[Head(queue).from] = 0
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, cap>>

Reconfigure(nc) ==
    /\ nc \in CapVals
    /\ cap' = nc
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, queue>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f, t \in Fridges : Enqueue(f, t)
    \/ Process
    \/ DropHead
    \/ \E nc \in CapVals : Reconfigure(nc)

CONSTANTS
  Fridges = {1, 2, 3}
  InitTotal = 2
  CapVals = {1, 2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BloodUnitsConserved
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker manages units of blood held across several storage fridges and a bounded queue of pending transfer requests. Each transfer request names a source fridge and a destination fridge. The request queue applies backpressure: a new request is admitted only while the queue holds fewer requests than its current capacity. To process the request at the head of the queue, the tracker moves one unit from the source fridge to the destination, provided the source actually has a unit; if the source is empty the head request is dropped as unfulfillable. Blood units are only ever moved between fridges, never created or discarded, so the total number of units in the bank is fixed. The queue's capacity can be reconfigured at runtime as staffing changes. The danger is that a bug in processing a transfer could duplicate a unit or make one disappear, changing the bank's total.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of blood units summed across all fridges always equals the initial total.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m5p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Aircraft, Controllers, Quorum

VARIABLES votes, takeoffs, crashed
vars == <<votes, takeoffs, crashed>>

Range(s) == { s[i] : i \in DOMAIN s }

Init ==
    /\ votes = [ a \in Aircraft |-> {} ]
    /\ takeoffs = << >>
    /\ crashed = {}

Vote(c, a) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ a \notin Range(takeoffs)
    /\ votes' = [ votes EXCEPT ![a] = votes[a] \cup {c} ]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<takeoffs, crashed>>

Clear(a) ==
    /\ a \notin Range(takeoffs)
    /\ Cardinality(votes[a] \ crashed) >= Quorum
    /\ takeoffs' = Append(takeoffs, a)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, takeoffs>>

Recover(c) ==
    /\ c \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, takeoffs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, a \in Aircraft : Vote(c, a)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Clear(a)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Recover(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleTakeoff ==
    \A a \in Aircraft :
        Cardinality({ i \in DOMAIN takeoffs : takeoffs[i] = a }) <= 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Aircraft = {p1, p2}
  Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
  Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleTakeoff
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator clears aircraft for takeoff, an irreversible action: once an aircraft is cleared and rolls, that clearance cannot be taken back, and each aircraft must be cleared at most once. Every clearance must be backed by a quorum of tower controllers who vote for that specific aircraft. Controllers cast votes for aircraft that have not yet been cleared; an aircraft is cleared once it has collected at least the quorum number of votes from controllers who are currently on duty, and the clearance is appended to an immutable takeoff log. Any one controller can crash silently, and a crashed controller's votes no longer count toward a quorum; a crashed controller may later come back on duty. The danger is that a race in the voting could clear the same aircraft for takeoff twice, sending it down the runway on two separate clearances.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no aircraft is ever cleared for takeoff more than once in the takeoff log.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m9p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Updates, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES version, history, stagedA, stagedB, epoch
vars == <<version, history, stagedA, stagedB, epoch>>

Idle == [busy |-> FALSE, id |-> CHOOSE u \in Updates : TRUE, base |-> 0, snap |-> {}]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ history = {}
    /\ stagedA = Idle
    /\ stagedB = Idle
    /\ epoch = 0

StageA(u) ==
    /\ ~ stagedA.busy
    /\ stagedA' = [busy |-> TRUE, id |-> u, base |-> version, snap |-> history]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, history, stagedB, epoch>>

StageB(u) ==
    /\ ~ stagedB.busy
    /\ stagedB' = [busy |-> TRUE, id |-> u, base |-> version, snap |-> history]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, history, stagedA, epoch>>

CommitA ==
    /\ stagedA.busy
    /\ stagedA.base = version
    /\ stagedA.id \notin history
    /\ history' = stagedA.snap \cup {stagedA.id}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ stagedA' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stagedB, epoch>>

CommitB ==
    /\ stagedB.busy
    /\ stagedB.base = version
    /\ stagedB.id \notin history
    /\ history' = stagedB.snap \cup {stagedB.id}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ stagedB' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stagedA, epoch>>

RejectA ==
    /\ stagedA.busy
    /\ (stagedA.base # version \/ stagedA.id \in history)
    /\ stagedA' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, history, stagedB, epoch>>

RejectB ==
    /\ stagedB.busy
    /\ (stagedB.base # version \/ stagedB.id \in history)
    /\ stagedB' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, history, stagedA, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ version' = 0
    /\ history' = {}
    /\ stagedA' = Idle
    /\ stagedB' = Idle

Next ==
    \/ \E u \in Updates : StageA(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : StageB(u)
    \/ CommitA
    \/ CommitB
    \/ RejectA
    \/ RejectB
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RecordVersionConsistent == Cardinality(history) = version
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Updates = {u1, u2}
  MaxEpoch = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RecordVersionConsistent
nl:
A container-ship crane yard keeps one shared stow-plan record that two independent crane controllers both update. Each controller works optimistically: it stages an update by capturing a snapshot of the current record together with the record's version number, then later tries to commit it. A commit succeeds only if the record's version is still the one the controller captured (so nothing has changed underneath it) and the update it carries is not already in the record; on success the controller writes back its snapshot plus its new entry and bumps the version. If the version has moved on, or the entry is already present, the staged update is rejected and must be re-staged against a fresh snapshot. From time to time the yard performs an epoch-numbered reconfiguration, which starts a fresh stow plan: it bumps the epoch, resets the record and its version, and discards any staged updates. The danger is a lost update, where one controller's stale snapshot overwrites the record and silently drops an entry another controller had already committed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the record's version number always equals the number of distinct entries currently in the record.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m4p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Orders, Slots, Cap

VARIABLES queue, grants, crashed
vars == <<queue, grants, crashed>>

SlotTaken(s) == \E g \in grants : g.slot = s
OrderHasSlot(o) == \E g \in grants : g.order = o

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ crashed = FALSE

Enqueue(o, s) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [order |-> o, slot |-> s])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, crashed>>

Process ==
    /\ ~ crashed
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ ~ SlotTaken(Head(queue).slot)
    /\ ~ OrderHasSlot(Head(queue).order)
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {[slot |-> Head(queue).slot, order |-> Head(queue).order]}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

DropHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ (SlotTaken(Head(queue).slot) \/ OrderHasSlot(Head(queue).order))
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, crashed>>

Release(g) ==
    /\ g \in grants
    /\ grants' = grants \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ ~ crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, grants>>

Recover ==
    /\ crashed
    /\ crashed' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, grants>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : Enqueue(o, s)
    \/ Process
    \/ DropHead
    \/ \E g \in grants : Release(g)
    \/ Crash
    \/ Recover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleSlot == Cardinality(grants) = Cardinality({ g.slot : g \in grants })
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Orders = {o1, o2}
  Slots = {1, 2}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleSlot
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction assigns numbered priority slots to incoming orders. Order-entry requests, each naming an order and the slot it wants, arrive into a single bounded intake queue that applies backpressure and refuses new requests when it is full. A matching-engine worker processes the request at the head of the queue: if the requested slot is currently unallocated and the order does not already hold a slot, the worker grants that slot to that order and removes the request. If the requested slot is already taken or the order already holds a slot, the head request is dropped. The matching worker can crash silently at any moment, after which no requests are processed until it recovers; enqueuing and dropping continue meanwhile. An order may also release its slot, freeing it for reallocation. The danger is that some interleaving lets the same priority slot be granted to two different orders at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no priority slot is ever granted to more than one order at the same time.
